column3: Production web server in VPC-PROD cannot access internet. yum update failing. Instance i-0abc123 in subnet-prod-private-1a.
column4: Root cause: NAT Gateway was deleted during cleanup. Resolution: Created new NAT Gateway nat-0xyz789 in public subnet. Updated route table rtb-prod-private to point 0.0.0.0/0 to new NAT GW. Verified connectivity restored.

column3: Application APP-ORDER-SVC cannot connect to RDS database orders-prod. Connection timeout after 30 seconds. Started after security group changes.
column4: Root cause: Security group sg-rds-prod was modified and removed inbound rule from application SG. Resolution: Added inbound rule allowing TCP 3306 from sg-app-order-svc. Connection restored immediately.

column3: Services in VPC-PROD cannot communicate with services in VPC-SHARED after VPC peering was set up. Ping and application traffic both failing.
column4: Root cause: Route tables were not updated in both VPCs. Resolution: Added route 10.1.0.0/16 -> pcx-abc123 in VPC-PROD route tables. Added route 10.0.0.0/16 -> pcx-abc123 in VPC-SHARED route tables. Also updated NACLs to allow traffic from peer CIDR ranges.

column2: EKS pods stuck in Pending state
column3: Multiple pods in namespace order-service stuck in Pending for over 30 minutes. Deployment scaled from 3 to 10 replicas but new pods not scheduling.
column4: Root cause: Node group reached maximum capacity (10 nodes). Insufficient CPU/memory for new pods. Resolution: Increased node group max size from 10 to 20. Cluster autoscaler provisioned 3 new nodes. Pods scheduled within 5 minutes.

column3: Pods failing to start with ImagePullBackOff error. Image: 123456789.dkr.ecr.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com/order-service:v2.3.1
column4: Root cause: Image tag v2.3.1 does not exist in ECR. Developer pushed as v2.3.1-hotfix but deployment manifest has v2.3.1. Resolution: Updated deployment manifest to correct tag v2.3.1-hotfix. Pods started successfully.

column3: Lambda function process-orders timing out after 15 seconds. SQS queue backing up with unprocessed messages.
column4: Root cause: Lambda was connecting to RDS in private subnet but VPC configuration was missing. Lambda had no route to RDS. Resolution: Configured Lambda VPC settings - added to private subnets with NAT Gateway access. Added Lambda SG to RDS inbound rules. Processing resumed.

column3: Application receiving AccessDenied when trying to write to s3://company-data-prod/reports/. Started after IAM policy update.
column4: Root cause: IAM policy was updated and s3:PutObject permission was accidentally removed. Resolution: Updated IAM policy to restore s3:PutObject permission for reports/* prefix. Verified application can write successfully.

column3: CPU utilization alarm for production ASG not triggering despite instances at 95% CPU for over 10 minutes.
column4: Root cause: Alarm was configured with wrong statistic (Average instead of Maximum) and wrong period (5 minutes instead of 1 minute). With 10 instances, average was below threshold. Resolution: Updated alarm to use Maximum statistic with 1-minute period. Alarm triggered correctly in next test.
